Fubara was tactically chosen to perform the unveiling and handover the flag of the All Progressives Congress, APC, to Hon Ogundu Kingsley Chinda, the anointed governorship candidate of Wike. Fubara did not only surrender his potential second term as a sitting governor to Chinda but also relinquished his role as the political leader of Rivers to Wike. The governor veered off the track of duty and handed down a stern warning, or so it seemed, to his organic supporters who stood by him in thick and thin during the dark moment of the political crisis in Rivers, telling them unreservedly that he was no more their leader. “Let me say something here so that it will always help us while we move forward”, he started. “I’m aware there are some issues where some persons who followed me when we had the crisis when you’re in your meeting you say ‘my leader, my leader’. “We are now in one house. And because we have one house, there is no issue about who is the leader. “I might be your oga (governor) but we have a common leader now. So, please, going forward, this issue of ‘my leader, my leader, my leader’, I want it resolved here and now.” There was a cumulus of silence at first, then a deafening applause. Governors as leaders Way back in January 2025, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, through his Vice, Kasim Shettima, had declared that all APC governors were political leaders of the party in their states. The implication is that as the highest political position in the state, a governor is seen as a leader politically. Tinubu made this known during the defection of Governor Agbu Kefas of Taraba State from PDP to APC. That pronouncement also covered Fubara the moment he defected from the same PDP to APC on December 9, 2025 and picked the 001 registration number of the ruling party. Also, shortly after Fubara’s defection, APC national leaders—including National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, and Deputy National Organising Secretary, Duru Eze, officially affirmed the Rivers governor as the leader of the APC in the state. They cited the APC Constitution, which designates sitting state governors as party leaders in their respective states. Rainbow/Fubara reconciliation Reeling in the deep cut injury occasioned by the over three years of political crisis that culminated into the declaration of a state of emergency on March 18, 2025 by President Tinubu, Wike and his political group soon realized the need to bring in Fubara and his structure to form a formidable force for 2027. Between August 16 and October 7, 2026, the Rainbow Coalition led by Wike held a back-to-back peace meeting with the governor in his private residence in Port Harcourt. The last meeting, expanded to include all the 23 LGA chairmen, had lawmakers from both state and national assemblies and political appointees loyal to Wike in attendance. At the meeting, Fubara accepted to return to the “family”. And the three suspended lawmakers loyal to him were reinstated while members of his political camp were promised juicy positions in the next dispensation. The peace meeting generated outrage in Rivers with many describing the governor as the “weakest” political leader in the history of Rivers. Fubara was alleged to have told his loyalists to go to the rural areas across the state and preach the gospel of Rainbow Coalition. State capture? Political observers are of the opinion that, having used his structure to propel Fubara to become governor, Wike was making a grand plan to capture the soul of the state. The internecine crisis witnessed in the past, obviously testified to the fact that the minister “was desperate for a third term by proxy”, said Franklin Uket, a public commentator. Uket noted that from the fight to regain his structure, “Wike never wanted Fubara to be independent minded as a governor. “He never wanted Fubara to draw any of his (Wike) political enemies close to his government”. Now politically suffocated, Fubara’s decision to throw in the towel of leadership also gives credence to the fact that the crisis is deeper than what appears in the surface. “The governor has been stampeded and bullied out of power”, Uket alleged. Ogbologwung said as a Rivers man, “I see the governor’s total surrender to Wike as a ship captain who swims ashore with the only life-buoy available during a wreck without bothering about the safety of his crew members. “The governor’s action has sadly demonstrated to the world how not to have a leader with a borrowed mind. “As a result, he has, by his own inconsiderate machinations deliberately sunk his political ship, having eaten to his own belle-full, that he desires less of neither the survival of his followers nor the state itself”. Wike has been begging Fubara since, it means that he wanted to take total power from Fubara. But we are waiting”. item.description: By Henry Umoru, Luminous Jannamike & Omeiza Ajayi With barely 77 days to the 2027 general elections, concerns over the preparedness of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, have become disturbing, especially following the discovery of artificial intelligence-generated photographs in the commission’s preliminary voters’ register. The development has raised fresh questions about the integrity of the electoral database, the effectiveness of INEC’s internal monitoring mechanisms and the commission’s capacity to conduct elections that would command public confidence. Accordingly, the worries have been compounded by complaints about other irregularities in the preliminary register, including questionable names, addresses, genders and photographs. Although INEC has acknowledged the problem and promised to clean up the register before the final version is released on December 15, 2026, the development has exposed vulnerabilities in the registration process. The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa, said the situation had moved beyond speculation following the commission’s admission that irregularities had occurred. He said: “This is quite concerning. This is no longer a rumour because even INEC Director of ICT came out to admit it.” Asogwa expressed concern that such a development was occurring under the leadership of the current INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, whom he described as a person with considerable academic and professional credentials. He said: “This is happening at a time when we have an INEC Chairman who is not just a lawyer, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria at that. If you look at his CV, he is also an academic of repute, an individual who was a Deputy Vice Chancellor of a University.” According to him, the proximity of the elections makes the development particularly disturbing. “That this is happening with less than 90 days to a crucial election is worrisome,” he added. On the commission’s preparedness, the LP spokesman said INEC was in the best position to assess and explain its readiness. However, he insisted that the commission had a responsibility to reassure Nigerians and rebuild confidence in the electoral process. He said: “As to their preparedness, the commission is in the best place to say. But we will suggest that they go back to the drawing board and inspire public confidence in the process. “Election also has a lot to do with public perception.” PDP: No cause for alarm However, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, adopted a different position, expressing confidence in the commission’s activities and urging political parties and other stakeholders not to make the discovery appear bigger than it is. The statement further said: “Over the years, Oba Olaitan has demonstrated a profound sincerity of purpose and the strategic capacity to champion the core interests of Afenifere while simultaneously promoting the greater unity of Nigeria. item.title: Eguavoen, CAF instructors at war over courses
item.description: Nigerian CAF instructors are up in arms against the NFF technical director, Austin Eguavoen over what they claimed as “unprofessional manner” he has been conducting a series of CAF D courses across the country. A majority of the 29 CAF instructors in Nigeria alleged that they have been sidelined from these courses and instead Eguavoen has been conducting the courses in Bayelsa, Edo, Delta, Ogun and Osun States with only Terry Eguaoje and one uncertified person. “W h a t Eguavoen is doing is very unprofessional,” one of the CAF instructors fired. “He has made the rest of us redundant even though we all are qualified to be part of these courses. “Instead, he is going around the country with only Dr Terry (Eguaoje) and one Fatai Akanji, who is not qualified to deliver papers at such courses. “Just how unprofessional can you be?” “These courses could be done across the country at the same time with some of us also being part of them,” added another CAF instructor. The tension between the instructors and Eguavoen has now reached a head that NIS DG Philip Shuaibu has waded into the crisis. This comes as a time that Eguavoen is seeking to stay on as NFF technical director following the expiration of his contract. item.description: The Normalisation Committee to spearhead major reform in Nigerian football has yet to be announced because several of the committee members recommended did not scale the FIFA integrity test. The NFF announced in an official statement on October 22 that world football governing body FIFA have approved a Normalisation Committee to reorganise football in the country following the resignation of the NFF executive committee led by Ibrahim Gusau. The statement pointed out that the committee members will be jointly appointed by FIFA and CAF. Since then not much has been reported on this development. A top source has now informed that the delay in the announcement of this committee has been held back because several of the proposed members did not pass the integrity test conducted by FIFA. “Some of those recommended for the committee did not pass the FIFA test, that is partly why the committee is not yet in place, ” a top source said. “However, I wouldn’t want to give out the names of those who did not scale through.” It was further gathered that the committee will have between seven and nine members with strong indications that there could be as many as two non-Nigerians on it. Meanwhile, a former NFF general secretary as well as a one-time highly influential NFF executive committee member are among those lobbying to head the Normalisation Committee. The committee will be expected to round up by May 31, 2027. The post Normalisation C’ttee: Recommended members fail FIFA integrity test appeared first on Vanguard News .

A comedian once said that President Kwame Nkrumah once visited Nigeria and as he drove in a convoy with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, he saw a man urinating by the roadside. He castigated Nigerians for being dirty. Balewa felt chagrined, despondent and crestfallen. He quickly organised a reciprocal visit to Ghana. As he drove in a convoy with President Nkrumah, he sighted a man defecating by the roadside. He quickly called Nkrumah’s attention to it. President Nkrumah, breaking protocol, asked the convoy to stop. He called for the arrest of the scoundrel and asked him: “Where are you from?” The man quickly retorted: “I AM FROM NIGERIA.” He immediately recalled the words of Mahatma Gandhi: “I can retain neither respect nor affection for a government which has been moving from wrong to wrong in order to defend its immorality.” What a shame! But the silent and salient point is to admonish our leaders and Nigerians on social courtesies, responsible waste disposal, provision of public toilets and efficient waste management. Comedy is a way of laughing at our all-embracing inadequacies. We must draw a clear-cut dichotomy between comperes, masters of ceremonies and comedians. The popular mistake is the desire of comedians to function as all of these. The popular compere, Collins Adeyemi, in his book _Director of Ceremony_, adumbrated on the need for differentiation to make professionalism the watchword. The Comedy Guild in Nigeria has become a fertile ground for youths, graduates and those with creative talents. They have become professional in their own right and a regular feature at private and public occasions. The field is robustly enriched with Warri (Wafi) and Sapele (Safa) boys and girls. Some of the notable comedians are Basket Mouth, I Go Die, Akpororo, Ali Baba, Gandoki, Rocky Feller, etc. Nigerian comedians have worked hard from the 1980s through the 1990s to the 2000s to lift comedy from gutter-snipe to professional level. They have become indispensable in the socio-economic and public calculus in Nigeria. WE WANT TO SEE MORE WOMEN COMEDIANS (COMEDIENNES). Henry Longfellow posited in ‘The Ladder of St. Augustine’ that “the heights by great men reached and kept were not attained by sudden flight, but they, while their companions slept, were toiling upward in the night.” Finally, Nigerian comedians have toiled all night and they deserve a place in the pantheon of great builders of Comedy/Drama/Theatre like Hubert Ogunde, Moses Olaiya (Baba Sala), Alawada, etc. They have to be more critical, spontaneous, authentic, creative and revolutionary in their drive to make Nigeria a better place. item.title: After Fasoranti: Can Afenifere bring the Yoruba together?
item.description: By Remi Ladigbolu The death of Pa Reuben Fasoranti has exposed a fundamental weakness in Yoruba political leadership. Despite a long tradition of political organisation and public service, the Yoruba lack an inclusive, broadly accepted structure capable of setting common priorities and sustaining a political direction. Organisations and factions claim to represent the same people, yet they often pursue separate courses, with no recognised platform to reconcile their differences or organise joint action. Fasoranti belonged to a political tradition shaped by Chief Obafemi Awolowo, Chief Adekunle Ajasin and Chief Abraham Adesanya. His standing helped hold Afenifere together through years of political uncertainty and internal division. His death raises a question that cannot be answered by choosing a successor alone. How can the Yoruba preserve their political inheritance without depending on another exceptional individual to hold them together? Afenifere is best placed to lead the search for an answer. But it must do more than fill Fasoranti’s position. It needs to resolve its own divisions and open its doors to the wider Yoruba community, including people and organisations with different political loyalties. Archbishop Emeritus Ayo Ladigbolu, chairman of the Yoruba Unity Forum and a member of the Afenifere Elders’ Caucus, addressed this problem at the South-West Stakeholders’ Dialogue in Akure on October 29 and 30, 2025. Organised by Afenifere with support from the Development Agenda for Western Nigeria Commission, the meeting considered governance, democracy and the region’s future. A starting point already exists within Afenifere. At its general meeting in Akure on January 24, 2024, the organisation abolished the positions of acting leader and deputy leader and established a 21-member Elders’ Caucus to advise its leader. Fasoranti chaired the caucus. Its members included Chief Ayo Adebanjo, Oba Olu Falae, Archbishop Emeritus Ayo Ladigbolu, the late Senator Cornelius Adebayo, Senator Femi Okunrounmu, Senator Kofo Bucknor-Akerele, Lieutenant-General Alani Akinrinade, Major-General Olu Bajowa, Professor Bolaji Akinyemi, Professor Banji Akintoye, Prince Tajudeen Olusi and Dr Kunle Olajide, amongst others. Those invited to participate must help shape the new arrangement, rather than being asked to endorse decisions already taken. The aim should be an Afenifere broad enough to accommodate different political tendencies while allowing participating organisations to retain their identities and independence. Its membership should draw on political experience, traditional institutions, scholarship, business, the professions, women and younger generations. Yoruba communities in Kwara and Kogi should also have a meaningful place. No faction or state should dominate the process. Leaders should be chosen for their integrity, experience and ability to work with people who disagree with them. Afenifere’s authority to articulate common Yoruba positions must rest on the confidence it earns, not on its history alone. Its chair should have a defined role, with major decisions taken through agreed procedures and responsibilities openly assigned. Security must be among its first priorities. Kidnapping, attacks on farming communities and the dangers faced by travellers in rural areas are undermining livelihoods and confidence in government. Afenifere should press for a coordinated regional response involving state governments, security agencies, traditional institutions and credible community organisations. The Oodua Peoples Congress, Agbekoya organisations and self-determination groups, including those associated with Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, should not be shut out of discussions about security and the grievances behind their activities. Afenifere could provide a political forum for these concerns and encourage cooperation within the law. The Aare Ona Kakanfo of Yorubaland also has a role to play, given the title’s historic association with Yoruba defence. The current holder, Iba Gani Adams, has experience engaging community security organisations. He could help bring groups together and convey their concerns to Afenifere, traditional rulers and state governments. Constitutional reform and regional economic cooperation should remain on the agenda. Afenifere could help develop common positions on federalism, regional autonomy and local government, while encouraging South-West states to cooperate on transport, agriculture, infrastructure and industry. Preserving Yoruba language, history and cultural heritage also requires sustained work by schools, universities, families and cultural institutions. Ladigbolu’s call for ethical renewal should apply to Afenifere itself. An organisation that demands integrity from public officials must account for its own decisions. It should publish a programme, assign responsibility for agreed goals and report on progress. The values it invokes must be evident in its conduct. Yoruba political history offers ample warning about the cost of division. The rupture between Awolowo and Chief Samuel Ladoke Akintola left deep scars. Later generations saw further disputes even as Ajasin, Adesanya, Bisi Onabanjo, Lateef Jakande, Bola Ige, Alfred Rewane and Fasoranti sustained different parts of the progressive tradition. The emergence of the Afenifere Renewal Group, the Yoruba Council of Elders, the Yoruba Unity Forum and self-determination movements reflects the range of interests any credible leadership arrangement must engage. Afenifere does not need to absorb every organisation or eliminate disagreement. It needs to provide a dependable forum where representatives can settle differences, identify areas of agreement and organise action around them. No faction owns the Yoruba political inheritance, and none can build a lasting platform by excluding those who disagree with it

item.content:encoded: By Bunmi Sofola BARBARA Taylor Bradford, renowned author of blockbusters like Woman of Substance and its sequel once said she was appalled by couples who row in public. She wrote: “When I open my mouth to say something, I edit my answer before it leaves my lips.” According to her, her husband, Bob, is a terrible time keeper who often wears clothes she loathes. But does she criticise him? No. She believes that would be showing a lack of respect. Instead, she suggested we should all bite our tongues and put our husbands on a pedestal. “She couldn’t have meant all that seriously, or at well over 80, she might be making her peace with the world after all those racy novels she’d written which had made her the millionaire she is today,” fumed Omorede a highly successful PR expert. “Why on earth would I want to put my husband on a pedestal when I simply don’t respect him?”, she wondered. “As a matter of fact, I disagree with virtually every word that comes out of his mouth, and the reason I feel this way towards Tony, my husband, stems from our very different backgrounds. I was born and bread in England and went to a private all girls’ convent school. I had a masters degree in business administration and worked in Ivy League establishments before I relocated to Nigeria. “In contrast, Tony was brought up in one of the down-market areas of Lagos by parents from a remote village in the West. And he has traits of his parents’ accent. At 46, he still revels in parochial slangs and uses hideous phrases in spite of my protest, which drives me mad. It’s so uncouth and sometimes makes me wonder how on earth we’ve ended up together. For although my husband is at least as bright as me and has a masters degree, to listen to his accent, you would think he worked as a market trader. And if he’s talking like a stall-owner in Ajegunle, how can I respect what he’s trying to tell me? “It’s not just his accent. Before working with the bank he now works for in a very senior position, he said he dreamt of being a musician and bragged he once played the drums with an obscure band that I never bothered to find out who the band leader was. And no topic is off limit to him. Recently, across the living room packed full of guests, I could hear Tony waxing lyrical to guests about the fantastic game of tennis he’d enjoyed that morning on Supersports. On and on he’d talk about volleys and drop shots, his commentary droning on and on often set my teeth on edge until I finally could bear it no longer. ‘Oh for heaven’s sake, can’t you stop going on about that hideous game?’ I asked. “It’s bad enough that you have to play it. Only dogs should be interested in ball games!” “As I glanced around the room, I could see our guests gaping at me. The look on their faces was all too obvious = how on earth could I be so rude to my husband? “But Tony just smiled. We’ve been married for six years and he’s used to me by now. But the truth is that, although I love him to bits, and we have a wonderful life with our children, I don’t respect him and he knows it. It is true that I was first attracted to Tony because he was so different to my first husband who left me for another woman. Chima, my ex, was the chief executive officer of a big company – a typical Alpha Male who commanded every room he stepped into. Tony, who I met a few years after our split, is quiet, unassuming and humble, he could not be more different. “And if you were to look at us, you certainly wouldn’t have put us together. I love to wear smart business designer clothes and Tony, in contrast, often has stubble when not at work, and wears more of native clothes. I think his style shows a lack of good taste and standards. How can I respect that? When I first met him, I was contracted to do a PR job for the bank he works with and had to work together with him. His kindness and gentle nature attracted him to me along with his creative skill. In addition, he’s unassuming and unflappable and I adored him for this. But however much I love him, I simply can’t respect him. Not only are his hobbies, accent and dress uncouth and immature, his political views are those of the Amala politics type. “I’m all for a world where the brightest get pushed to do even better. For Tony, the priority is ensuring that everyone is happy. Our biggest rows are about the children’s education. I attended private schools and want our children to attend the best – where they could learn to play the piano, etc. Tony, being government school-educated, doesn’t see the point. Any private school would do as long as they’re near the house and I despise his attitude that happiness is more important than qualifications. “It speaks for itself, doesn’t it, that if the children want something really useful – like help with their home-work – they come to me. Meanwhile, they’ll go to Tony for stints at the club or a fast-food joint. I know for sure I am too set in my ways to change. I believe the only quality we have in common is that we are both stubborn. Women of Barbara Taylor Bradford’s generation were brought up to tiptoe around their men, bite their tongues and keep the peace. I can’t think of anything more demeaning. I am convinced that far from being the way to a happy marriage – putting your husband on a pedestal is unhealthy, and treating everyone of his utterances like part of the Sermon on the Mount can only end in tears. “A lot of my friends have wondered: ‘Tony’s so nice, how can you be so rude to him?’ Howl hypocritical! Hardly any of them truly respect their husbands – and I know they all moan about them too. The only difference is that they do it behind their backs while I do it directly. Personally, I think they’re much more disloyal. Pretending that I respect Tony would make for a quieter life. But it wouldn’t made me happy. And what’s the point in being married if you’re not happy?! The Wife Wins All The Time? (Humour) A couple were so bored with their marriage that they decided to liven it up by competing against each other. But as the weeks went by, the husband became very depressed because his wife was always the winner of any game they played. One night at the club, his mate took pity on him and suggested a new game. “You can’t fail with this, Steve. It’s who can pee up the wall the highest. The bloke is bound to win.” The husband thought this was a great idea and rushed home to tell his wife. She agreed and they went out into the back yard to begin the competition. The wife dropped her knickers, lifted her leg and peed two feet up the wall. Confidently, the man undid his zip, took out his dick and was just about to start when his wife said, ‘Hold on, stop right there, no hands allowed!” The Husband Fights Back! (Humour) A couple are walking around the zoo when they come to the gorilla cage. There’s no one around, so the man says to his wife, “Sharon, take your blouse off and let’s see if it has any effect on the gorilla.” She hesitates. “Go on!” he urges, “no one will see”. So she takes the blouse off and the gorilla starts jumping up and down in excitement. “Now take your bra off,” he says. She does this and the gorilla gets even more excited. “Right, take your skirt off” he says. “Oh no, I couldn’t. How would we explain it if someone comes along?” She asks. “There’s no one around, it’ll be fine.” So, over the next few minutes the woman gradually takes all her clothes off and by this time, the gorilla is going berserk. Then the husband opens the door of the cage and pushes her inside. “Now, tell him you have a headache!” he says. item.title: Some actors don’t love fame; they just love acting – Lolade Okusanya
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress and The Unserious Podcast co-host Lolade Okusanya has said some actors are more interested in their craft than the fame that comes with it. Okusanya made this observation while discussing celebrity privacy on the podcast, citing veteran actresses Genevieve Nnaji and Omotola Jalade Ekeinde as examples of public figures who have sought a more private life despite their fame. “There are people like Genevieve; after all the fame, they went back into their shells. They still have the fame, but they want to go back into their shells. Omotola Jalade Ekeinde too, she went back into her shell,” she said. According to the actress, celebrities may desire privacy, but public attention can make it difficult for them to maintain personal boundaries. She noted that fans may still approach celebrities for photographs when they encounter them in public, regardless of their preference for a quieter life. “Because no matter how much she still craves that private life, we will disrupt it,” Okusanya said. She added that not every actor is motivated by the prospect of fame, explaining that some are primarily passionate about acting itself. “Some actors do not love fame; they just love acting. But some jobs come with fame,” she said. Her comments highlight the tension between public recognition and personal privacy in the entertainment industry, where professional visibility can make it difficult for celebrities to maintain a life away from public attention. item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Destiny does not always play fair. Sometimes, it goes overboard or hits below the belt. It is convenient to see Burna Boy today as the “African Giant” without paying much attention to the circumstances that brought the moniker about. It was, in fact, a controversy that Damini Ogulu, popularly known as Burna Boy, took advantage of after feeling diminished and disrespected. Burna Boy’s “African Giant” moniker originated from a 2019 controversy over the size of his name on the Coachella music festival’s promotional poster. What began as a protest against how he was billed eventually became the title of his breakthrough album and a defining identity in his career. Yet, in retrospect, destiny was playing fair, with an all-seeing eye. In response to the perceived disrespect, he took to social media to assert his stature, describing himself as an “African Giant”. The statement attracted considerable attention, with some Nigerians criticising him as arrogant, while others supported his insistence that African musicians deserved greater recognition. If respect is earned rather than demanded, Burna Boy is an exception. He demanded it and earned it. His achievements on the global stage as an African artiste tell the whole story, and 2026 has been a stupendous year for the *Twice as Tall* global hitmaker. In less than one week, he has recorded two historic firsts: performing at the NFL’s first regular-season game in France and becoming the first Nigerian artiste to present an award at the Ballon d’Or. These milestones follow his World Cup feat, where he performed alongside Colombian superstar Shakira at the first-ever halftime show at a FIFA World Cup final, helping bring Afrobeats to one of football’s biggest global stages. Burna Boy also made history as the first Afrobeats artiste to perform on the Grammy Awards stage. His performance featured Brandy and 21 Savage, marking a significant moment for the genre at the prestigious US music ceremony. In July 2023, Burna Boy became the first African artiste to sell out a stadium in the United States when he performed at Citi Field in New York. The milestone demonstrated the commercial appeal of African music in the American live-music market. In the same vein, Burna Boy headlined the 80,000-capacity London Stadium during his *Love, Damini* tour, becoming the first African artiste to headline the venue. The concert was another landmark for African performers in the United Kingdom. The appearance placed Nigerian music before a huge international football audience. He further joined Tems and Rema for a performance at the NBA All-Star Game halftime show in Salt Lake City, Utah. item.title: There’s more to women than sexuality – Bukola Ikuomola
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Actress and filmmaker Bukola Ikuomola, popularly known as MZNicollet, has said women should be recognised for their intellect, achievements and contributions to society rather than their sexuality. In a chat with Potpourri, Ikuomola, who expressed her views on women flaunting their sexuality on social media, said she admired women who distinguished themselves through their intelligence and accomplishments. “There is more to women than sexuality. I admire women who are known for their intellect and other great achievements,” she said. The Ondo State-born actress, who also has Urhobo roots in Warri, Delta State, said she developed a passion for acting from an early age and had always admired the profession. She is a graduate of Novena University, Ogume, Delta State, and also runs Nickiscollections as its chief executive officer. Speaking about the sacrifices she has made to build her acting career, Ikuomola said she had invested considerable time, effort and the little money available to her in improving her craft. She described working with veteran actors, including Saheed Balogun, Jobola Dabo, Ayo Mogaji and Muyiwa Ademola, as some of her memorable experiences in the industry. She also expressed pride in producing her first movie, *Enemy Within*. On the kind of roles she enjoys playing, Ikuomola said she preferred heroic characters who demonstrate strength and determination and contribute meaningfully to a story. However, she noted that her versatility allows her to approach different roles with passion. The actress said her ambition was to become a megastar with an international reputation, extending her influence beyond Nollywood. On relationships, Ikuomola said respect and a good sense of humour were qualities she valued in a man, adding that she preferred men to make the first move. She also declared a preference for money over love, explaining that past experiences had left her feeling used in relationships because of how much she gave to the people she loved. “Now I go for money. And if love comes with it, I grab it too,” she said, adding that love becomes sweeter when money is involved. item.title: How Real Warri Pikin conquered comedy stages across continents
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi When Nigerian comedian and actor Anita Alaire Asuoha, popularly known as Real Warri Pikin, won the Best Stand-Up Comedian award at the 2026 African Muzik Magazine Awards (AFRIMMA), it marked another milestone in a career built on hard work, persistence and an unmistakable brand of humour. The honour, presented at the awards ceremony held in Dallas, Texas, on September 12, placed her ahead of several established comedy stars, including Basketmouth, Bovi, Godfrey, Eric Omondi, Trevor Noah, Patrick “Salvado” Idringi and Ty Ngachira. Her victory was a significant recognition of her growing influence in African comedy and her expanding international profile. <u> </u> “This award means a lot to me because it is a recognition of the journey, the work and the years of showing up even when I didn’t know where it would lead,” she said. “To be recognised as Best Comedian at AFRIMMA, representing Nigeria and Africa, is a huge honour. It also reminds me that staying true to who you are and using your story to connect with people can take you places you never imagined,” she added. For Asuoha, the AFRIMMA triumph represents more than a trophy. It reflects years of building an entertainment career that spans stand-up comedy, acting, digital content creation, live shows and television and web productions. Known for her energetic stage presence, Warri-inflected expressions and use of Nigerian Pidgin, Real Warri Pikin has developed a comic identity rooted in everyday experiences, relationships and the peculiarities of Nigerian life. item.title: Mixed reactions trail Zlatan’s wedding
item.description: By Sarah Ammah Nigerian street-pop star Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael, popularly known as Zlatan Ibile, has sparked conversations online following his traditional wedding to his longtime partner, Davita Lamai, in Lagos on October 24, 2026. The glamorous ceremony attracted celebrities, including singer Davido, who served as one of the groomsmen. The couple impressed guests with their traditional outfits and colourful cultural displays, making the celebration a major talking point on social media. While many fans congratulated the couple and praised their outfits, others focused on Davita’s appearance, with some social media users making negative comments about her looks. Another issue that generated debate was Zlatan’s decision to marry Davita after they had already welcomed two children together. Some critics questioned why he chose to marry a woman who already had two children for him, while others defended the couple, arguing that their relationship and decision to marry were nobody else’s business. The wedding also attracted attention following Nollywood actress Joke Jigan’s comments about the absence of popular “Lagos baddies” at the event, which generated mixed reactions online. Despite the criticism, many fans celebrated the couple’s union and praised Zlatan for taking the next step in his relationship with Davita. Ultimately, the wedding became more than a celebration of love, turning into a social media debate about beauty standards, relationships, marriage and public opinion. item.title: Chacx, African China collaborate on ‘Forgive’
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nigerian singer Chacx has collaborated with veteran musician African China on his new single, Forgive, released on Friday, October 30. The collaboration brings the emerging singer together with African China, known for his street-inspired music and socially conscious themes. Speaking about the collaboration, Chacx expressed excitement about working with the veteran singer, describing the experience as an opportunity to learn from an established voice in Nigerian music. “Working with African China is an exciting experience for me. I have great respect for his journey and the connection his music has built with audiences over the years. Collaborating with him gave me an opportunity to exchange creative ideas and approach the song from different perspectives. I believe working with artistes from different generations can broaden your understanding of music and challenge you to grow. I am glad to have him on Forgive and look forward to listeners experiencing what we have created together,” Chacx said. Chacx, whose real name is Manu Charles Chukwuye, began his professional music career in 2019 with Obi Mo, featuring Cme2k. His subsequent releases include the EPs New Beginning (2021) and Advanced (2023), alongside songs such as Blessed, featuring Portable and Shocker Lo Se Beat, Hold Me, Baby Girl, Feelings and Fake Friends. In 2026, he signed with Homeboy International Music Label, adding another development to his career. With Forgive, Chacx brings his sound together with African China’s established musical identity in a collaboration that introduces a new release to both artistes’ catalogues. item.description: German police and protesters clashed across the country Saturday following massive youth-led protests, with authorities using water cannon and pepper spray as masked demonstrators hurled fireworks, stones and bottles. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined protests nationwide that were organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police were pelted with projectiles in the western city of Frankfurt, and responded by using water cannon and pepper spray as they sought to clear protesters. “Incidents of stones and fireworks being thrown at the emergency services continue to occur,” police said on X. “We are taking action against these troublemakers.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. ‘Boiling Point’ In Berlin, a protest that was not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. item.title: Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident
item.description: The Katsina State Government has dismissed reports linking the incident that occurred in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to Governor Dikko Radda’s Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign, describing such claims as false and misleading. In a statement, the government said preliminary findings showed that the disturbance stemmed from a disagreement between participants in a Maulud procession and security personnel over designated procession routes, resulting in confusion along a public street in Yankara. It stressed that the incident was entirely unrelated to thegovernor’s campaign activities or the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally held in Faskari. According to the government, Governor Radda passed through Yankara without incident on his way to Faskari, where he paid a courtesy visit to the District Head’s Palace and was received by the district head and other traditional rulers. The governor, it said, later proceeded to the Faskari Local Government secretariat, where he inspected ongoing renovation works at the secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally and interacting with residents and supporters. Governor Dikko Radda addresses a crowd of supporters at the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign in Faskari Local Government Area of Katsina State on October 31, 2026. The state government urged relevant security agencies to carry out a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that those responsible are identified where necessary. In the statement signed by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ibrahim Mohammed, the government appealed to residents to remain calm, uphold peace, and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary tension. Violence was reported in Yankara town on Saturday after suspected hoodlums attacked supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), leaving several people injured and a campaign vehicle set ablaze. Eyewitnesses said the attackers allegedly ambushed APC supporters heading to Governor Radda’s campaign rally in Faskari, disrupting movement along the major road and causing panic among residents. Angry youths were also alleged to have blocked the route the campaign convoy was expected to use. item.title: Africa’s First Ever Youth Olympics Open In Senegal
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, opened Saturday in the Senegalese capital, marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are omnipresent across Dakar, which is hosting nearly 2,700 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event will see the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the young athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “Today it’s not just a nation that is welcoming the Youth Olympic Games; it’s an entire continent that is opening its arms”, Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye told a sport and development summit Saturday ahead of the Games’ opening ceremony. Senegal’s Influencer and TikToker Khaby Lame carries the Youth Olympic Flame on the eve of the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on October 30, 2026. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly, located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events.
